BROKER PLACEMENT AGREEMENT
This Broker Placement Agreement (the “Agreement”) is entered into as of September 2, 2022, by and
between Alder Point Partners (“Company”), with offices in Sacramento, California, and Bellhaven
Advisory (“Broker”), with offices in Denver, Colorado.
1. Engagement
Company engages Broker, on a non-exclusive basis, to market and broker placements of renewable
energy tax credits issued under the Coastal Solar Credit Program in Company’s active markets,
including but not limited to Oregon, Washington, and California.
2. Broker Representations and Warranties
Broker represents and warrants that it holds, or will hold prior to soliciting any placement, all licenses,
registrations, and other authorizations required under applicable state and federal law to broker
renewable energy tax credits in each jurisdiction in which it operates on Company’s behalf.
3. Fees
Company shall pay Broker a placement fee equal to a percentage of the gross value of each credit
placement, as set forth in Schedule A (attached separately).
4. Term and Termination
This Agreement is effective as of the date first written above and continues until terminated by either
party upon thirty (30) days’ written notice.
5. Signatures
For Bellhaven Advisory:  Derek Holt, Managing Director
For Alder Point Partners:  Tom Reyes, Land Acquisition Manager

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK
 PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM
TO:  Elena Marlowe, Chief Executive Officer
FROM:  John Ellery, Head of Legal
DATE:  October 4, 2022
RE:  Coastal Solar Credit Program — Regulatory Exposure Assessment
I. Background
At your request, this memorandum summarizes the current regulatory exposure of the Coastal Solar
Credit Program based on our review to date. This analysis is provided as legal advice and is protected
by the attorney-client privilege and/or attorney work product doctrine.
II. Land Eligibility Documentation
Our review of conservation easement filings for a subset of parcels submitted with Coastal Solar credit
applications identified acreage figures that do not reconcile with the corresponding county filings. This
issue was first flagged internally by Alder Point personnel in March 2022 and has not, to our
knowledge, been resolved.
III. Broker Licensing Status
Bellhaven Advisory’s broker registration renewal in Oregon and Washington remains unresolved.
Bellhaven has represented that marketing in those states should pause until renewal clears; our
understanding is that marketing has continued.
IV. Regulatory Risk
Continued marketing and credit placement activity while these two issues remain open increases the
risk of regulatory scrutiny, including potential exposure under state broker licensing statutes and federal
tax credit eligibility rules.
V. Recommendation
We recommend pausing new Coastal Solar placements until (1) land eligibility documentation is
reconciled against county records, and (2) Bellhaven’s broker registration status in all active states is
confirmed current.

 PRODUCT
PRELIMINARY ASSESSMENT
TO:  Elena Marlowe, Robert Denniston
FROM:  John Ellery, Head of Legal
DATE:  February 21, 2023
RE:  Preliminary Assessment — Anonymous Complaint Received February 20, 2023
Prepared in anticipation of potential regulatory inquiry.
I. Summary of Complaint
On February 20, 2023, Compliance received an anonymous complaint alleging that Coastal Solar credit
applications include land parcels that do not meet conservation eligibility requirements.
II. Preliminary Findings
The allegations are consistent with land eligibility documentation concerns previously identified
internally (see privileged memorandum dated October 4, 2022) and not fully resolved as of this date.
III. Anticipated Regulatory Inquiry
Given the nature of the allegations and the tax-credit structure of the Coastal Solar program, a
governmental inquiry (state or federal) is a reasonably foreseeable outcome.
IV. Recommendation
We recommend engaging outside counsel immediately to conduct an independent internal review
under privilege, rather than waiting for a regulatory inquiry to be received.

At Alder Point Partners’ request, GreenAcre Land Survey Co. conducted an independent acreage

Findings
Four of eight parcels (NW-1051, NW-1052, NW-1071, NW-1093) show reported acreage that exceeds
the corresponding county filing acreage by 12–18%. We recommend these parcels be re-verified
against original survey records before further reliance on the reported figures.
The remaining four parcels are consistent with county records within normal survey tolerance.

 PRODUCT
INTERIM FINDINGS MEMORANDUM
TO:  John Ellery, Head of Legal, Cascade Timber Holdings
FROM:  Grace Lin, Partner, L&L Associates
DATE:  March 10, 2023
RE:  Coastal Solar Credit Program — Internal Review, Interim Findings
I. Scope
This interim memorandum summarizes our review to date of custodian communications relating to the
anonymous complaint received February 20, 2023.
II. Findings
Custodian communications indicate that land parcel eligibility concerns were raised internally as early
as March 2022 and again in June 2022, and that a privileged risk assessment recommending a pause
in new placements was provided to leadership in October 2022. Placements continued.
Communications also indicate that Bellhaven Advisory’s broker registration gap in Oregon and
Washington was known internally at Bellhaven prior to disclosure to Alder Point, and that marketing
continued in those states during the gap.
III. Next Steps
We recommend continuing custodian collection, applying the agreed search term set, and preparing a
privilege log in parallel with substantive review.

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
WITNESS INTERVIEW MEMORANDUM
TO: File / Grace Lin, Partner, L&L Associates
FROM: Alan Brooks, Paralegal, L&L Associates
DATE: July 24, 2023
RE: Interview of Hannah Cole, Land Records Administrator, Cascade Timber Holdings - conducted July 21,
2023
I. Purpose
This memorandum summarizes the witness interview conducted on July 21, 2023 at the direction of counsel in
connection with the internal review of the Coastal Solar Credit Program and the allegations received February 20, 2023.
The interview was conducted so that counsel may render legal advice to Cascade Timber Holdings. This memorandum
reflects the mental impressions, conclusions, and opinions of counsel's agents and is protected work product.
II. Summary of Interview
Ms. Cole has served as Land Records Administrator since 2019. She maintains the conservation easement files
supporting credit applications submitted by Alder Point Partners on the Company's behalf. Key points:
1. Parcel files were assembled from county recorder downloads and field notes provided by Alder Point. Ms. Cole did
not independently verify acreage against county records before files were transmitted to Alder Point.
2. In March 2022, Ms. Cole noticed that acreage figures in four of the eight Northwest-batch parcel files did not match
the county easement filings. She raised the discrepancy with Alder Point's land acquisition team (T. Reyes) and was told
the county records were 'catching up' to amended surveys.
3. Ms. Cole did not escalate the discrepancy to Cascade Timber management or to the compliance team because the
parcels were administered by Alder Point and she understood verification to be Alder Point's responsibility under the
partnership agreement.
4. She recalls a re-survey of two Klamath County parcels in mid-2022 that reduced reported acreage; the original figures
had already been used in submitted credit applications.
III. Assessment
Ms. Cole appeared credible and cooperative. Her account corroborates the timeline in the complaint and is consistent
with the GreenAcre survey findings. Her statement that she raised the discrepancy in March 2022 establishes notice on
the Alder Point side at an early date.
IV. Follow-Up Items
1. Obtain the March 2022 correspondence between Ms. Cole and T. Reyes.
2. Obtain the Klamath County re-survey files.
3. Prepare supplemental questions for a second interview (see G. Lin comments).

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
L&L ASSOCIATES
Outside Counsel - Attorneys at Law
July 27, 2023
VIA EMAIL
Dana Whitaker, CPA/CFF
Principal
Whitaker Forensic Accounting
Re: Engagement of Whitaker Forensic Accounting - Assistance to Counsel (Kovel)
Dear Ms. Whitaker:
This letter confirms the engagement of Whitaker Forensic Accounting ("you" or "the Firm") by L&L Associates ("we" or
"outside counsel") to assist us in rendering legal advice to our client, Cascade Timber Holdings, in connection with the
internal review of the Coastal Solar Credit Program and related litigation that we reasonably anticipate.
You will perform forensic accounting analysis of parcel payment records, credit sale proceeds, and related
disbursements identified by counsel. Your work will be performed solely at our direction and for the purpose of enabling
us to provide legal advice to our client; you will not provide accounting, audit, or tax services to Cascade Timber
Holdings directly.
All communications between you and this Firm, and all work papers, analyses, and deliverables prepared in connection
with this engagement, are confidential and are intended to be protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work
product doctrine, consistent with the principles of United States v. Kovel. You will deliver all work product exclusively to
this Firm, will mark all deliverables 'Privileged & Confidential - Prepared at the Direction of Counsel,' and will not
communicate regarding this engagement with any third party, including the client, without our prior instruction.
Fees will be billed to and paid by this Firm per the attached rate schedule. Please countersign and return this letter to
confirm.
Sincerely,
Grace Lin
Partner, L&L Associates

LARSEN TAX ADVISORY
Tax Provision & Compliance Services
TO: Craig Sato, Controller, Cascade Timber Holdings
FROM: Owen Larsen, Principal, Larsen Tax Advisory
DATE: August 22, 2023
RE: Q3 FY2023 Tax Provision - Deferred Revenue and Contingencies
I. Scope
This memorandum supports the Company's Q3 FY2023 tax provision. It was prepared for financial reporting purposes at
the request of the Controller under our standard engagement terms. It does not constitute legal advice, and we
understand it may be produced in the ordinary course of the Company's financial statement audit.
II. Deferred Revenue - Credit Program Pause
With new Coastal Solar credit placements paused as of late June 2023, deferred revenue of approximately $2.1M
associated with undelivered placements should remain classified as a contract liability until delivery or refund. We
concur with management's proposed treatment.
III. Contingencies
We understand the Company is responding to an IRS examination related to the Coastal Solar Credit Program. No
reserve is proposed at this time because management cannot reasonably estimate an outcome. If the examination
results in credit disallowances, prior-year positions may require adjustment. This memorandum addresses provision
treatment only and expresses no view on the merits.
IV. Conclusion
Provision entries as proposed are consistent with ASC 740. Please contact us with questions.

Strategic Communications & Investor Messaging
Coastal Solar Program Pause - Investor Messaging One-Pager
Prepared for: Frank Delgado, VP Investor Relations, Cascade Timber Holdings
August 8, 2023 - DRAFT v2 - For internal discussion purposes only
Key Messages
1. Cascade Timber has voluntarily paused new Coastal Solar credit placements while it completes a routine internal
review of program documentation.
2. Existing placements are unaffected; the Company continues to service all outstanding credits.
3. The pause reflects strong governance, not a change in the fundamentals of the timberlands business.
Anticipated Investor Q&A
Q: Was the pause requested by a regulator?
A: The pause is a Company decision as part of standard program governance. We do not comment on regulatory
matters.
Q: What is the revenue impact?
A: Q3 impact is immaterial to consolidated results; see the Q3 board pack for segment detail.
Q: When will placements resume?
A: We will provide an update when the internal review is complete.
Tone Guidance
Confident, factual, non-speculative. Do not characterize the scope or findings of the internal review. Route any media
inquiry mentioning the IRS or a subpoena to Legal before responding.

Clearwater Land LLC (Owner) and Alder Point Partners (Optionee) - Klamath County, Oregon - Alder parcel
ref. KW-o02
This Option Agreement (this "Agreement") is made effective as of September 20, 2022 (the "Effective
Date”) by and between CLEARWATER LAND LLC, an Oregon limited liability company ("Owner"),
and ALDER POINT PARTNERS, with offices in Sacramento, California ("Optionee"). Owner and
Optionee are each a "Party".
RECITALS
A. Owner is the owner of certain real property in Klamath County, Oregon, located east of U.S.
Highway 97 (the "Route 97 corridor"), containing approximately 111.87 acres according to the records
of the Klamath County Assessor, and more particularly described in Exhibit A (together with all
easements, rights and appurtenances, the "Property").
B. The Property adjoins other land of Owner to the north, which is the subject of a separate option
agreement being negotiated between the Parties. This Agreement is independent of that agreement.
C. Optionee wishes to obtain, and Owner is willing to grant, an exclusive option to purchase the
Property on the terms of this Agreement.
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the Option Fee and the mutual covenants below, the Parties
agree as follows:
1. Grant of Option
1.1 Owner grants to Optionee the exclusive and irrevocable option to purchase the Property on the
terms of this Agreement (the "Option”).
2. Option Term; Extension
2.1 The Option Term begins on the Effective Date and ends at 5:00 p.m. Pacific time on the day that is
twelve (12) months after the Effective Date (the "Option Term").
2.2 Optionee may extend the Option Term once, for an additional period of six (6) months (the
“Extension Period"), by written notice to Owner given before the Option Term expires, provided that
each Option Payment then due has been paid or deferred under Section 3.3. References in this
Agreement to the Option Term include any Extension Period.
3. Option Fee and Option Payments
3.1 In consideration of the Option, Optionee shall pay Owner an option fee of Twelve Thousand Dollars
($12,000) (the "Option Fee"), in installments (each, an "Option Payment”) as set out in Schedule 1
below.
3.2 Option Payments shall be made by check or by wire transfer to an account designated by Owner in
writing.
3.3 Optionee may, by written notice to Owner given on or before the due date of any Option Payment
other than the Initial Option Payment, defer that Option Payment to a later date stated in the notice,
which date shall be no later than the last day of the Option Term. Any Option Payment not paid by the

last day of the Option Term is due on that day.
3-4 Optionee may prepay all or any part of the Option Fee at any time without premium or penalty.
3-5 Option Payments, once made, are non-refundable except as provided in Sections 6 and 10, and shall
be credited against the Purchase Price at Closing.
Schedule 1 — Option Payments

4. Purchase Price
4.1 The purchase price for the Property is $1,150 per acre of Net Acreage (the "Purchase Price"),
payable in cash at Closing, less the Option Payments made.
4-2 "Net Acreage" means the gross acreage of the Property as shown on the Survey, excluding any area
within public road rights-of-way. The Assessor acreage stated in the Recitals and in Exhibit A is for
identification only and is not a representation by either Party of Net Acreage.
5- Due Diligence; Survey
5.1 During the Option Term, Optionee and its consultants may enter the Property on reasonable prior
notice to Owner to conduct boundary and topographic surveys, soil, environmental and siting studies
and similar investigations, at Optionee's expense. Optionee shall repair any damage caused by its entry
and shall indemnify Owner against third-party claims arising from it.
5-2 Optionee may obtain a boundary survey of the Property by a land surveyor licensed in Oregon (the
"Survey").
5-3 Within fifteen (15) days after the Effective Date, Owner shall deliver to Optionee copies of any
leases, surveys, title reports and recorded instruments affecting the Property that are in Owner's
possession or control.
6. Title
6.1 Optionee may obtain a preliminary title report for the Property and shall notify Owner of any
objections within thirty (30) days after receiving it. Owner shall notify Optionee within ten (10) days
whether Owner will cure each objection. If Owner does not agree to cure an objection, Optionee may
waive it or terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be refunded to
Optionee.
6.2 Owner discloses that the Property, together with Owner's adjoining land, is subject of record to a
grazing lease recorded in 1994 in Volume M94, Page 18832, Records of Klamath County, Oregon (the
“Grazing Lease"), Owner represents that the Grazing Lease has expired by its terms and that no person
holds grazing rights on the Property under it. No release of the Grazing Lease has been located of
record. Before Closing, Owner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and record a release
APP-OPT form rev. 2022-1 - exec Page 2
Clearwater Land LLC / Alder Point Partners + Option Agreement (KW-02) — Confidential

or quitclaim of the Grazing Lease from the lessee or its successors. If no release is recorded before
Closing, Optionee may (a) waive this requirement, (b)-extend Closing by up to sixty (60) days to allow it
to be recorded, or (c) terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be
refunded to Optionee.
7. Owner's Covenants j
7.1 During the Option Term, Owner shall not sell, lease, encumber or grant any interest in the Property,
or permit any lien to attach to it, without Optionee's prior written consent; provided that Owner and its
members may continue the existing agricultural and grazing use of the Property until Closing, so long
as that use does not interfere with Optionee’s investigations under Section 5.
: 7.2 Owner shall keep the Property in its present condition, ordinary wear and natural causes excepted.
8. Exercise of Option
8.1 Optionee may exercise the Option at any time during the Option Term by written notice to Owner
(the "Exercise Notice"). If the Option is not exercised before the Option Term expires, the Option shall
lapse and Owner shall retain the Option Payments made.
9. Closing ;
9.1 Closing of the purchase shall occur through escrow with a title company in Klamath County, Oregon
selected by Optionee, on a date designated by Optionee not later than sixty (60) days after the Exercise
Notice ("Closing").
9.2 At Closing, Owner shall convey the Property to Optionee or its assignee by statutory warranty deed,
subject only to exceptions approved or waived under Section 6. Owner shall pay the premium for a
standard owner's policy of title insurance; escrow fees shall be shared equally; real property taxes shall
be prorated as of Closing. At Closing, Owner shall grant to Optionee, by recordable instrument, a
non-exclusive, perpetual easement for ingress, egress and utilities over the existing ranch track where it
crosses Owner's adjoining land to the north, running from the county road to the Property.
10. Termination; Default
10.1 Optionee may terminate this Agreement at any time by written notice to Owner. Owner shall retain
the Option Payments made through the date of termination, except where termination results from
Owner's default or a title failure under Section 6.
10.2 If Optionee fails to make an Option Payment when due (as it may be deferred under Section 3.3),
Owner may give Optionee written notice of the failure. If the payment is not made within ten (10) days
after that notice, Owner may terminate this Agreement by further written notice.
10.3 If Owner fails to perform under this Agreement, Optionee may seek specific performance or
terminate this Agreement and recover all Option Payments made.
11. Memorandum of Option
11.1 On request of either Party, the Parties shall sign a memorandum of this Agreement in recordable
form, which Optionee may record in the Official Records of Klamath County, Oregon.
12. Assignment
12.1 Optionee may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any affiliate of Optionee or to any
successor to Optionee's land acquisition business, on written notice to Owner. Owner may not assign
this Agreement without Optionee's written consent.

overnight courier, or by email with a copy by first-class mail, to the addresses below (or another

14. Governing Law; Venue
14.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Oregon. Any action arising under this
Agreement shall be brought in the Circuit Court of the State of Oregon for Klamath County.
15. Miscellaneous
15.1 This Agreement is the entire agreement of the Parties regarding the Property and may be amended
only in a writing signed by both Parties. Time is of the essence. This Agreement may be signed in
counterparts, and signatures delivered by scanned copy are effective as originals.
15.2 BEFORE SIGNING OR ACCEPTING THIS INSTRUMENT, THE PERSON TRANSFERRING FEE
TITLE SHOULD INQUIRE ABOUT THE PERSON'S RIGHTS, IF ANY, UNDER ORS 195.300, 195.301
AND 195.305 TO 195.336. THIS INSTRUMENT DOES NOT ALLOW USE OF THE PROPERTY IN
VIOLATION OF APPLICABLE LAND USE LAWS AND REGULATIONS (ORS 93.040).
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have signed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

Clearwater Land LLC (Owner) and Alder Point Partners (Optionee)  ·  Klamath County, Oregon  ·  Alder parcel ref. KW-01

This Option Agreement (this "Agreement") is made effective as of [____________________] (the "Effective Date") by and between CLEARWATER LAND LLC, an Oregon limited liability company ("Owner"), and ALDER POINT PARTNERS, with offices in Sacramento, California ("Optionee"). Owner and Optionee are each a "Party".

RECITALS

A. Owner is the owner of certain real property in Klamath County, Oregon, located east of U.S. Highway 97 (the "Route 97 corridor"), containing approximately 148.62 acres according to the records of the Klamath County Assessor, and more particularly described in Exhibit A (together with all easements, rights and appurtenances, the "Property").

B. The Property adjoins other land of Owner to the south, which is the subject of a separate option agreement being negotiated between the Parties. This Agreement is independent of that agreement.

C. Optionee wishes to obtain, and Owner is willing to grant, an exclusive option to purchase the Property on the terms of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the Option Fee and the mutual covenants below, the Parties agree as follows:

1. Grant of Option

1.1 Owner grants to Optionee the exclusive and irrevocable option to purchase the Property on the terms of this Agreement (the "Option").

2. Option Term; Extension

2.1 The Option Term begins on the Effective Date and ends at 5:00 p.m. Pacific time on the day that is twelve (12) months after the Effective Date (the "Option Term").

2.2 Optionee may extend the Option Term once, for an additional period of six (6) months (the "Extension Period"), by written notice to Owner given before the Option Term expires, provided that each Option Payment then due has been paid or deferred under Section 3.3. References in this Agreement to the Option Term include any Extension Period.

3. Option Fee and Option Payments

3.1 In consideration of the Option, Optionee shall pay Owner an option fee of Twelve Thousand Dollars ($12,000) (the "Option Fee"), in installments (each, an "Option Payment") as set out in Schedule 1 below.

3.2 Option Payments shall be made by check or by wire transfer to an account designated by Owner in writing.

3.3 Optionee may, by written notice to Owner given on or before the due date of any Option Payment other than the Initial Option Payment, defer that Option Payment to a later date stated in the notice, which date shall be no later than the last day of the Option Term. Any Option Payment not paid by the last day of the Option Term is due on that day.

3.4 Optionee may prepay all or any part of the Option Fee at any time without premium or penalty.

3.5 Option Payments, once made, are non-refundable except as provided in Sections 6 and 10, and shall be credited against the Purchase Price at Closing.

5. Due Diligence; Survey

Optionee shall repair any damage caused by its entry and shall indemnify Owner against third-party claims arising from it.

5.2 Optionee may obtain a boundary survey of the Property by a land surveyor licensed in Oregon (the "Survey").

5.3 Within fifteen (15) days after the Effective Date, Owner shall deliver to Optionee copies of any leases, surveys, title reports and recorded instruments affecting the Property that are in Owner's possession or control.

6. Title

6.1 Optionee may obtain a preliminary title report for the Property and shall notify Owner of any objections within thirty (30) days after receiving it. Owner shall notify Optionee within ten (10) days whether Owner will cure each objection. If Owner does not agree to cure an objection, Optionee may waive it or terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be refunded to Optionee.

6.2 Owner discloses that the Property, together with Owner's adjoining land, is subject of record to a grazing lease recorded in 1994 in Volume M94, Page 18832, Records of Klamath County, Oregon (the "Grazing Lease"). Owner represents that the Grazing Lease has expired by its terms and that no person holds grazing rights on the Property under it. No release of the Grazing Lease has been located of record. Before Closing, Owner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and record a release or quitclaim of the Grazing Lease from the lessee or its successors. 7. Owner's Covenants

7.1 During the Option Term, Owner shall not sell, lease, encumber or grant any interest in the Property, or permit any lien to attach to it, without Optionee's prior written consent; provided that Owner and its members may continue the existing agricultural and grazing use of the Property until Closing, so long as that use does not interfere with Optionee's investigations under Section 5.

7.2 Owner shall keep the Property in its present condition, ordinary wear and natural causes excepted.

8. Exercise of Option

8.1 Optionee may exercise the Option at any time during the Option Term by written notice to Owner (the "Exercise Notice"). If the Option is not exercised before the Option Term expires, the Option shall lapse and Owner shall retain the Option Payments made.

9. Closing

9.1 Closing of the purchase shall occur through escrow with a title company in Klamath County, Oregon selected by Optionee, on a date designated by Optionee not later than ninety (90) days after the Exercise Notice ("Closing").

9.2 At Closing, Owner shall convey the Property to Optionee or its assignee by statutory warranty deed, subject only to exceptions approved or waived under Section 6. Owner shall pay the premium for a standard owner's policy of title insurance; escrow fees shall be shared equally; real property taxes shall be prorated as of Closing.

10. Termination; Default

10.1 Optionee may terminate this Agreement at any time by written notice to Owner. Owner shall retain the Option Payments made through the date of termination, except where termination results from Owner's default or a title failure under Section 6.

10.2 If Optionee fails to make an Option Payment when due (as it may be deferred under Section 3.3), Owner may give Optionee written notice of the failure. If the payment is not made within ten (10) days after that notice, Owner may terminate this Agreement by further written notice.

10.3 If Owner fails to perform under this Agreement, Optionee may seek specific performance or terminate this Agreement and recover all Option Payments made.

11. Memorandum of Option

11.1 On request of either Party, the Parties shall sign a memorandum of this Agreement in recordable form, which Optionee may record in the Official Records of Klamath County, Oregon.

12. Assignment

12.1 Optionee may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any affiliate of Optionee or to any successor to Optionee's land acquisition business, on written notice to Owner. Owner may not assign this Agreement without Optionee's written consent.

13. Notices

13.1 Notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with a copy by first-class mail, to the addresses below (or another address a Party designates by notice):

To Owner: Clearwater Land LLC, Attn: Gordon L. Pruitt, Managing Member, P.O. Box 1187, Klamath Falls, Oregon 97601; with a copy to Margaret A. Oyler, Oyler & Beck LLP, 412 Main Street, Klamath Falls, Oregon 97601

To Optionee: Alder Point Partners, Attn: Tom Reyes, Land Acquisition Manager, Sacramento, California; email: treyes@alderpointpartners.com

14. Governing Law; Venue

14.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Oregon. Any action arising under this Agreement shall be brought in the Circuit Court of the State of Oregon for Klamath County.

15. Miscellaneous

15.1 This Agreement is the entire agreement of the Parties regarding the Property and may be amended only in a writing signed by both Parties. Time is of the essence. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, and signatures delivered by scanned copy are effective as originals.

15.2 BEFORE SIGNING OR ACCEPTING THIS INSTRUMENT, THE PERSON TRANSFERRING FEE TITLE SHOULD INQUIRE ABOUT THE PERSON'S RIGHTS, IF ANY, UNDER ORS 195.300, 195.301 AND 195.305 TO 195.336. THIS INSTRUMENT DOES NOT ALLOW USE OF THE PROPERTY IN VIOLATION OF APPLICABLE LAND USE LAWS AND REGULATIONS (ORS 93.040).

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have signed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

Alder Point PartnersLand Acquisition  ·  Sacramento, California

Option Agreement

Clearwater Land LLC (Owner) and Alder Point Partners (Optionee)  ·  Klamath County, Oregon  ·  Alder parcel ref. KW-01

This Option Agreement (this "Agreement") is made effective as of [____________], 2022 (the "Effective Date") by and between CLEARWATER LAND LLC, an Oregon limited liability company ("Owner"), and ALDER POINT PARTNERS, with offices in Sacramento, California ("Optionee"). Owner and Optionee are each a "Party".

RECITALS

A. Owner is the owner of certain real property in Klamath County, Oregon, located east of U.S. Highway 97 (the "Route 97 corridor"), containing approximately 148.62 acres according to the records of the Klamath County Assessor, and more particularly described in Exhibit A (together with all easements, rights and appurtenances, the "Property").

B. The Property adjoins other land of Owner to the south, which is the subject of a separate option agreement being negotiated between the Parties. This Agreement is independent of that agreement.

C. Optionee wishes to obtain, and Owner is willing to grant, an exclusive option to purchase the Property on the terms of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the Option Fee and the mutual covenants below, the Parties agree as follows:

1. Grant of Option

1.1 Owner grants to Optionee the exclusive and irrevocable option to purchase the Property on the terms of this Agreement (the "Option").

2. Option Term; Extension

2.1 The Option Term begins on the Effective Date and ends at 5:00 p.m. Pacific time on the day that is twelve (12) months after the Effective Date (the "Option Term").

2.2 Optionee may extend the Option Term once, for an additional period of six (6) months (the "Extension Period"), by written notice to Owner given before the Option Term expires, provided that each Option Payment then due has been paid or deferred under Section 3.3. References in this Agreement to the Option Term include any Extension Period.

3. Option Fee and Option Payments

3.1 In consideration of the Option, Optionee shall pay Owner an option fee of Twelve Thousand Dollars ($12,000) (the "Option Fee"), in installments (each, an "Option Payment") as set out in Schedule 1 below.

3.2 Option Payments shall be made by check or by wire transfer to an account designated by Owner in writing.

3.3 Optionee may, by written notice to Owner given on or before the due date of any Option Payment other than the Initial Option Payment, defer that Option Payment to a later date stated in the notice.

3.4 Optionee may prepay all or any part of the Option Fee at any time without premium or penalty.

3.5 Option Payments, once made, are non-refundable except as provided in Sections 6 and 10, and shall be credited against the Purchase Price at Closing.

Schedule 1 — Option Payments

Option Payment

Amount

Due (subject to Sections 3.3 and 3.4)

Initial Option Payment

$4,000

Within ten (10) business days after the Effective Date

Second Option Payment

$4,000

On or before the 180th day after the Effective Date

Third Option Payment

$4,000

On or before the 270th day after the Effective Date

Total Option Fee

$12,000

4. Purchase Price

4.1 The purchase price for the Property is $1,150 per acre of Net Acreage (the "Purchase Price"), payable in cash at Closing, less the Option Payments made.

4.2 "Net Acreage" means the gross acreage of the Property as shown on the Survey, excluding any area within public road rights-of-way. The Assessor acreage stated in the Recitals and in Exhibit A is for identification only and is not a representation by either Party of Net Acreage.

5. Due Diligence; Survey

5.1 During the Option Term, Optionee and its consultants may enter the Property on reasonable prior notice to Owner to conduct boundary and topographic surveys, soil, environmental and siting studies and similar investigations, at Optionee's expense. Optionee shall repair any damage caused by its entry and shall indemnify Owner against third-party claims arising from it.

5.2 Optionee may obtain a boundary survey of the Property by a land surveyor licensed in Oregon (the "Survey").

5.3 Within fifteen (15) days after the Effective Date, Owner shall deliver to Optionee copies of any leases, surveys, title reports and recorded instruments affecting the Property that are in Owner's possession or control.

6. Title

6.1 Optionee may obtain a preliminary title report for the Property and shall notify Owner of any objections within thirty (30) days after receiving it. Owner shall notify Optionee within ten (10) days whether Owner will cure each objection. If Owner does not agree to cure an objection, Optionee may waive it or terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be refunded to Optionee.

6.2 Owner discloses that the Property, together with Owner's adjoining land, is subject of record to a grazing lease recorded in 1994 in Volume M94, Page 18832, Records of Klamath County, Oregon (the "Grazing Lease"). Owner represents that the Grazing Lease has expired by its terms and that no person holds grazing rights on the Property under it. No release of the Grazing Lease has been located of record. Before Closing, Owner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and record a release or quitclaim of the Grazing Lease from the lessee or its successors. If no release is recorded before Closing, Optionee may (a) waive this requirement, (b) extend Closing by up to sixty (60) days to allow it to be recorded, or (c) terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be refunded to Optionee.

7. Owner's Covenants

7.1 During the Option Term, Owner shall not sell, lease, encumber or grant any interest in the Property, or permit any lien to attach to it, without Optionee's prior written consent.

7.2 Owner shall keep the Property in its present condition, ordinary wear and natural causes excepted.

8. Exercise of Option

8.1 Optionee may exercise the Option at any time during the Option Term by written notice to Owner (the "Exercise Notice"). If the Option is not exercised before the Option Term expires, the Option shall lapse and Owner shall retain the Option Payments made.

9. Closing

9.1 Closing of the purchase shall occur through escrow with a title company in Klamath County, Oregon selected by Optionee, on a date designated by Optionee not later than sixty (60) days after the Exercise Notice ("Closing").

9.2 At Closing, Owner shall convey the Property to Optionee or its assignee by statutory warranty deed, subject only to exceptions approved or waived under Section 6. Owner shall pay the premium for a standard owner's policy of title insurance; escrow fees shall be shared equally; real property taxes shall be prorated as of Closing.

10. Termination; Default

10.1 Optionee may terminate this Agreement at any time by written notice to Owner. Owner shall retain the Option Payments made through the date of termination, except where termination results from Owner's default or a title failure under Section 6.

10.2 If Optionee fails to make an Option Payment when due (as it may be deferred under Section 3.3), Owner may give Optionee written notice of the failure. If the payment is not made within ten (10) days after that notice, Owner may terminate this Agreement by further written notice.

10.3 If Owner fails to perform under this Agreement, Optionee may seek specific performance or terminate this Agreement and recover all Option Payments made.

11. Memorandum of Option

11.1 On request of either Party, the Parties shall sign a memorandum of this Agreement in recordable form, which Optionee may record in the Official Records of Klamath County, Oregon.

12. Assignment

12.1 Optionee may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any affiliate of Optionee or to any successor to Optionee's land acquisition business, on written notice to Owner. Owner may not assign this Agreement without Optionee's written consent.

13. Notices

13.1 Notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with a copy by first-class mail, to the addresses below (or another address a Party designates by notice):

To Owner: Clearwater Land LLC, Attn: Gordon L. Pruitt, Managing Member, P.O. Box 1187, Klamath Falls, Oregon 97601

To Optionee: Alder Point Partners, Attn: Tom Reyes, Land Acquisition Manager, Sacramento, California; email: treyes@alderpointpartners.com

14. Governing Law; Venue

14.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Oregon. Any action arising under this Agreement shall be brought in the Circuit Court of the State of Oregon for Klamath County.

15. Miscellaneous

15.1 This Agreement is the entire agreement of the Parties regarding the Property and may be amended only in a writing signed by both Parties. Time is of the essence. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, and signatures delivered by scanned copy are effective as originals.

15.2 BEFORE SIGNING OR ACCEPTING THIS INSTRUMENT, THE PERSON TRANSFERRING FEE TITLE SHOULD INQUIRE ABOUT THE PERSON'S RIGHTS, IF ANY, UNDER ORS 195.300, 195.301 AND 195.305 TO 195.336. THIS INSTRUMENT DOES NOT ALLOW USE OF THE PROPERTY IN VIOLATION OF APPLICABLE LAND USE LAWS AND REGULATIONS (ORS 93.040).

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have signed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

to be recorded, or (c) terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be
refunded to Optionee.

7.1 During the Option Term, Owner shall not sell, lease, encumber or grant any interest in the Property,

members may continue the existing agricultural and grazing use of the Property until Closing, so long
as that use does not interfere with Optionee’s investigations under Section 5.
: 7.2 Owner shall keep the Property in its present condition, ordinary wear and natural causes excepted.
8. Exercise of Option
8.1 Optionee may exercise the Option at any time during the Option Term by written notice to Owner
(the "Exercise Notice"). If the Option is not exercised before the Option Term expires, the Option shall
lapse and Owner shall retain the Option Payments made.
9. Closing ;
9.1 Closing of the purchase shall occur through escrow with a title company in Klamath County, Oregon
selected by Optionee, on a date designated by Optionee not later than sixty (60) days after the Exercise
Notice ("Closing").
9.2 At Closing, Owner shall convey the Property to Optionee or its assignee by statutory warranty deed,
subject only to exceptions approved or waived under Section 6. Owner shall pay the premium for a
standard owner's policy of title insurance; escrow fees shall be shared equally; real property taxes shall
be prorated as of Closing. At Closing, Owner shall grant to Optionee, by recordable instrument, a
non-exclusive, perpetual easement for ingress, egress and utilities over the existing ranch track where it
crosses Owner's adjoining land to the north, running from the county road to the Property.
10. Termination; Default
10.1 Optionee may terminate this Agreement at any time by written notice to Owner. Owner shall retain
the Option Payments made through the date of termination, except where termination results from
Owner's default or a title failure under Section 6.
10.2 If Optionee fails to make an Option Payment when due (as it may be deferred under Section 3.3),
Owner may give Optionee written notice of the failure. If the payment is not made within ten (10) days
after that notice, Owner may terminate this Agreement by further written notice.
10.3 If Owner fails to perform under this Agreement, Optionee may seek specific performance or
terminate this Agreement and recover all Option Payments made.
11. Memorandum of Option
11.1 On request of either Party, the Parties shall sign a memorandum of this Agreement in recordable
form, which Optionee may record in the Official Records of Klamath County, Oregon.
12. Assignment
12.1 Optionee may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any affiliate of Optionee or to any
successor to Optionee's land acquisition business, on written notice to Owner. Owner may not assign
this Agreement without Optionee's written consent.

Option Agreement

Clearwater Land LLC (Owner) and Alder Point Partners (Optionee)  ·  Klamath County, Oregon  ·  Alder parcel ref. KW-02

This Option Agreement (this "Agreement") is made effective as of [____________], 2022 (the "Effective Date") by and between CLEARWATER LAND LLC, an Oregon limited liability company ("Owner"), and ALDER POINT PARTNERS, with offices in Sacramento, California ("Optionee"). Owner and Optionee are each a "Party".

RECITALS

A. Owner is the owner of certain real property in Klamath County, Oregon, located east of U.S. Highway 97 (the "Route 97 corridor"), containing approximately 111.87 acres according to the records of the Klamath County Assessor, and more particularly described in Exhibit A (together with all easements, rights and appurtenances, the "Property").

B. The Property adjoins other land of Owner to the north, which is the subject of a separate option agreement being negotiated between the Parties. This Agreement is independent of that agreement.

C. Optionee wishes to obtain, and Owner is willing to grant, an exclusive option to purchase the Property on the terms of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the Option Fee and the mutual covenants below, the Parties agree as follows:

1. Grant of Option

1.1 Owner grants to Optionee the exclusive and irrevocable option to purchase the Property on the terms of this Agreement (the "Option").

2. Option Term; Extension

2.1 The Option Term begins on the Effective Date and ends at 5:00 p.m. Pacific time on the day that is twelve (12) months after the Effective Date (the "Option Term").

2.2 Optionee may extend the Option Term once, for an additional period of six (6) months (the "Extension Period"), by written notice to Owner given before the Option Term expires, provided that each Option Payment then due has been paid or deferred under Section 3.3. References in this Agreement to the Option Term include any Extension Period.

3. Option Fee and Option Payments

3.1 In consideration of the Option, Optionee shall pay Owner an option fee of Twelve Thousand Dollars ($12,000) (the "Option Fee"), in installments (each, an "Option Payment") as set out in Schedule 1 below.

3.2 Option Payments shall be made by check or by wire transfer to an account designated by Owner in writing.

3.3 Optionee may, by written notice to Owner given on or before the due date of any Option Payment other than the Initial Option Payment, defer that Option Payment to a later date stated in the notice.

3.4 Optionee may prepay all or any part of the Option Fee at any time without premium or penalty.

3.5 Option Payments, once made, are non-refundable except as provided in Sections 6 and 10, and shall be credited against the Purchase Price at Closing.

Schedule 1 — Option Payments

Option Payment

Amount

Due (subject to Sections 3.3 and 3.4)

Initial Option Payment

$4,000

Within ten (10) business days after the Effective Date

Second Option Payment

$4,000

On or before the 180th day after the Effective Date

Third Option Payment

$4,000

On or before the 270th day after the Effective Date

Total Option Fee

$12,000

4. Purchase Price

4.1 The purchase price for the Property is $1,150 per acre of Net Acreage (the "Purchase Price"), payable in cash at Closing, less the Option Payments made.

4.2 "Net Acreage" means the gross acreage of the Property as shown on the Survey, excluding any area within public road rights-of-way. The Assessor acreage stated in the Recitals and in Exhibit A is for identification only and is not a representation by either Party of Net Acreage.

5. Due Diligence; Survey

5.1 During the Option Term, Optionee and its consultants may enter the Property on reasonable prior notice to Owner to conduct boundary and topographic surveys, soil, environmental and siting studies and similar investigations, at Optionee's expense. Optionee shall repair any damage caused by its entry and shall indemnify Owner against third-party claims arising from it.

5.2 Optionee may obtain a boundary survey of the Property by a land surveyor licensed in Oregon (the "Survey").

5.3 Within fifteen (15) days after the Effective Date, Owner shall deliver to Optionee copies of any leases, surveys, title reports and recorded instruments affecting the Property that are in Owner's possession or control.

6. Title

6.1 Optionee may obtain a preliminary title report for the Property and shall notify Owner of any objections within thirty (30) days after receiving it. Owner shall notify Optionee within ten (10) days whether Owner will cure each objection. If Owner does not agree to cure an objection, Optionee may waive it or terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be refunded to Optionee.

6.2 Owner discloses that the Property, together with Owner's adjoining land, is subject of record to a grazing lease recorded in 1994 in Volume M94, Page 18832, Records of Klamath County, Oregon (the "Grazing Lease"). Owner represents that the Grazing Lease has expired by its terms and that no person holds grazing rights on the Property under it. No release of the Grazing Lease has been located of record. Before Closing, Owner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and record a release or quitclaim of the Grazing Lease from the lessee or its successors. If no release is recorded before Closing, Optionee may (a) waive this requirement, (b) extend Closing by up to sixty (60) days to allow it to be recorded, or (c) terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be refunded to Optionee.

7. Owner's Covenants

7.1 During the Option Term, Owner shall not sell, lease, encumber or grant any interest in the Property, or permit any lien to attach to it, without Optionee's prior written consent.

7.2 Owner shall keep the Property in its present condition, ordinary wear and natural causes excepted.

8. Exercise of Option

8.1 Optionee may exercise the Option at any time during the Option Term by written notice to Owner (the "Exercise Notice"). If the Option is not exercised before the Option Term expires, the Option shall lapse and Owner shall retain the Option Payments made.

9. Closing

9.1 Closing of the purchase shall occur through escrow with a title company in Klamath County, Oregon selected by Optionee, on a date designated by Optionee not later than sixty (60) days after the Exercise Notice ("Closing").

9.2 At Closing, Owner shall convey the Property to Optionee or its assignee by statutory warranty deed, subject only to exceptions approved or waived under Section 6. Owner shall pay the premium for a standard owner's policy of title insurance; escrow fees shall be shared equally; real property taxes shall be prorated as of Closing. [Access: Owner to confirm where the ranch track from the county road runs and whether it crosses Owner's land to the north. Add access easement if needed.]

10. Termination; Default

10.1 Optionee may terminate this Agreement at any time by written notice to Owner. Owner shall retain the Option Payments made through the date of termination, except where termination results from Owner's default or a title failure under Section 6.

10.2 If Optionee fails to make an Option Payment when due (as it may be deferred under Section 3.3), Owner may give Optionee written notice of the failure. If the payment is not made within ten (10) days after that notice, Owner may terminate this Agreement by further written notice.

10.3 If Owner fails to perform under this Agreement, Optionee may seek specific performance or terminate this Agreement and recover all Option Payments made.

11. Memorandum of Option

11.1 On request of either Party, the Parties shall sign a memorandum of this Agreement in recordable form, which Optionee may record in the Official Records of Klamath County, Oregon.

12. Assignment

12.1 Optionee may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any affiliate of Optionee or to any successor to Optionee's land acquisition business, on written notice to Owner. Owner may not assign this Agreement without Optionee's written consent.

13. Notices

13.1 Notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with a copy by first-class mail, to the addresses below (or another address a Party designates by notice):

To Owner: Clearwater Land LLC, Attn: Gordon L. Pruitt, Managing Member, P.O. Box 1187, Klamath Falls, Oregon 97601

To Optionee: Alder Point Partners, Attn: Tom Reyes, Land Acquisition Manager, Sacramento, California; email: treyes@alderpointpartners.com

14. Governing Law; Venue

14.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Oregon. Any action arising under this Agreement shall be brought in the Circuit Court of the State of Oregon for Klamath County.

15. Miscellaneous

15.1 This Agreement is the entire agreement of the Parties regarding the Property and may be amended only in a writing signed by both Parties. Time is of the essence. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, and signatures delivered by scanned copy are effective as originals.

15.2 BEFORE SIGNING OR ACCEPTING THIS INSTRUMENT, THE PERSON TRANSFERRING FEE TITLE SHOULD INQUIRE ABOUT THE PERSON'S RIGHTS, IF ANY, UNDER ORS 195.300, 195.301 AND 195.305 TO 195.336. THIS INSTRUMENT DOES NOT ALLOW USE OF THE PROPERTY IN VIOLATION OF APPLICABLE LAND USE LAWS AND REGULATIONS (ORS 93.040).

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have signed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

4. Purchase Price
4.1 The purchase price for the Property is $1,150 per acre of Net Acreage (the "Purchase Price"),
payable in cash at Closing, less the Option Payments made.
4-2 "Net Acreage" means the gross acreage of the Property as shown on the Survey, excluding any area
within public road rights-of-way. The Assessor acreage stated in the Recitals and in Exhibit A is for
identification only and is not a representation by either Party of Net Acreage.
5- Due Diligence; Survey
5.1 During the Option Term, Optionee and its consultants may enter the Property on reasonable prior
notice to Owner to conduct boundary and topographic surveys, soil, environmental and siting studies
and similar investigations, at Optionee's expense. Optionee shall repair any damage caused by its entry
and shall indemnify Owner against third-party claims arising from it.
5-2 Optionee may obtain a boundary survey of the Property by a land surveyor licensed in Oregon (the
"Survey").
5-3 Within fifteen (15) days after the Effective Date, Owner shall deliver to Optionee copies of any
leases, surveys, title reports and recorded instruments affecting the Property that are in Owner's
possession or control.
6. Title
6.1 Optionee may obtain a preliminary title report for the Property and shall notify Owner of any
objections within thirty (30) days after receiving it. Owner shall notify Optionee within ten (10) days
whether Owner will cure each objection. If Owner does not agree to cure an objection, Optionee may
waive it or terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be refunded to
Optionee.
6.2 Owner discloses that the Property, together with Owner's adjoining land, is subject of record to a
grazing lease recorded in 1994 in Volume M94, Page 18832, Records of Klamath County, Oregon (the
“Grazing Lease"), Owner represents that the Grazing Lease has expired by its terms and that no person
holds grazing rights on the Property under it. No release of the Grazing Lease has been located of
record. Before Closing, Owner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and record a release

or quitclaim of the Grazing Lease from the lessee or its successors. If no release is recorded before
Closing, Optionee may (a) waive this requirement, (b)-extend Closing by up to sixty (60) days to allow it
to be recorded, or (c) terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be
refunded to Optionee.
7. Owner's Covenants j
7.1 During the Option Term, Owner shall not sell, lease, encumber or grant any interest in the Property,
or permit any lien to attach to it, without Optionee's prior written consent; provided that Owner and its
members may continue the existing agricultural and grazing use of the Property until Closing, so long
as that use does not interfere with Optionee’s investigations under Section 5.
: 7.2 Owner shall keep the Property in its present condition, ordinary wear and natural causes excepted.
8. Exercise of Option
8.1 Optionee may exercise the Option at any time during the Option Term by written notice to Owner
(the "Exercise Notice"). If the Option is not exercised before the Option Term expires, the Option shall
lapse and Owner shall retain the Option Payments made.
9. Closing ;
9.1 Closing of the purchase shall occur through escrow with a title company in Klamath County, Oregon
selected by Optionee, on a date designated by Optionee not later than sixty (60) days after the Exercise
Notice ("Closing").
9.2 At Closing, Owner shall convey the Property to Optionee or its assignee by statutory warranty deed,
subject only to exceptions approved or waived under Section 6. Owner shall pay the premium for a
standard owner's policy of title insurance; escrow fees shall be shared equally; real property taxes shall
be prorated as of Closing. At Closing, Owner shall grant to Optionee, by recordable instrument, a
non-exclusive, perpetual easement for ingress, egress and utilities over the existing ranch track where it
crosses Owner's adjoining land to the north, running from the county road to the Property.
10. Termination; Default
10.1 Optionee may terminate this Agreement at any time by written notice to Owner. Owner shall retain
the Option Payments made through the date of termination, except where termination results from
Owner's default or a title failure under Section 6.
10.2 If Optionee fails to make an Option Payment when due (as it may be deferred under Section 3.3),
Owner may give Optionee written notice of the failure. If the payment is not made within ten (10) days
after that notice, Owner may terminate this Agreement by further written notice.
10.3 If Owner fails to perform under this Agreement, Optionee may seek specific performance or
terminate this Agreement and recover all Option Payments made.
11. Memorandum of Option
11.1 On request of either Party, the Parties shall sign a memorandum of this Agreement in recordable
form, which Optionee may record in the Official Records of Klamath County, Oregon.
12. Assignment
12.1 Optionee may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any affiliate of Optionee or to any
successor to Optionee's land acquisition business, on written notice to Owner. Owner may not assign
this Agreement without Optionee's written consent.

 CREDIT PURCHASE AGREEMENT
 Coastal Solar Credit Program — Bellhaven Advisory standard purchaser form
This Credit Purchase Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of [__________], 2022 (the
“Effective Date”), by and among Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc., an Oregon corporation with offices in
Portland, Oregon (“Seller”), acting through Alder Point Partners, with offices in Sacramento,
California, as administrator of the Coastal Solar Credit Program (“Administrator”); Cascade Pension
Partners, L.P., an Oregon limited partnership, with offices in Portland, Oregon (“Purchaser”); and,
solely for purposes of Sections 8 and 9, Bellhaven Advisory, with offices in Denver, Colorado
(“Placement Agent”).
RECITALS
A. Seller holds renewable energy tax credits issued under the Coastal Solar Credit Program (the
“Program”), which Administrator administers on Seller's behalf (the “Credits”).
B. Administrator has engaged Placement Agent, on a non-exclusive basis, to market and broker
placements of Credits under a Broker Placement Agreement dated as of September 2, 2022.
C. Purchaser wishes to purchase, and Seller wishes to sell, Credits in the Face Amount and at the price
set forth in Schedule 1, on the terms of this Agreement.
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set forth herein, the parties agree as
follows:
1. Definitions
“Face Amount” means the stated dollar value of a Credit as shown on its Credit Certificate. “Credit
Certificate” means the certificate issued under the Program evidencing a Credit. “Program
Documentation” means the Program description, investor deck, one-page summary, eligibility
checklist and eligibility screening materials prepared and furnished by Administrator, in the versions
approved by Administrator and delivered to Purchaser. “Closing” means the date on which Purchaser
pays the Aggregate Purchase Price. “Business Day” means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or bank
holiday in Portland, Oregon.
2. Purchase and Sale
Subject to the terms of this Agreement, Seller agrees to sell and Purchaser agrees to purchase Credits
having the aggregate Face Amount set forth in Schedule 1 (the “Purchased Credits”).
3. Purchase Price
The purchase price for the Purchased Credits is $0.89 per $1.00 of Face Amount (the “Unit Price”), for
an aggregate purchase price of $1,112,500 (the “Aggregate Purchase Price”), payable at Closing by wire
transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated in writing by Administrator.
Placement Agent's compensation is payable by Administrator under the Broker Placement Agreement
and is not payable by Purchaser.
4. Delivery of Credit Certificates
Within ten (10) Business Days after Closing, Administrator shall deliver to Purchaser, by electronic
transmission with originals to follow, Credit Certificates evidencing the Purchased Credits, each
identifying the certificate number, Program vintage, source parcel reference and Face Amount. Title to
and risk of the Purchased Credits pass to Purchaser upon delivery of the Credit Certificates. If any
Credit Certificate is not delivered within thirty (30) Business Days after Closing, Purchaser may, by

written notice, require refund of the portion of the Aggregate Purchase Price attributable to the

DECOVERAI · DISCOVERY REFERENCE

Attorney-client privilege definition

Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc.

Matter

IRS Examination — Coastal Solar Credit Program

Issued to

Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc., Attn: Legal Department, Portland, OR 97209

Issuing agency

Internal Revenue Service, Examination Division

Case no.

EX-2023-04471

Date issued

May 23, 2023

Response due

June 13, 2023 (21 days)

Revenue agent

Kevin Tran

Version

v1.0 — prepared July 16, 2026

I. Applicable matter

This definition applies to the IRS's examination of Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc. ("CTH" or "the Company") in connection with the Coastal Solar Credit Program (the "Program"), a renewable-energy / land-conservation tax credit program administered by Alder Point Partners and, for a period, brokered by Bellhaven Advisory.

"The Program" means the Coastal Solar Credit Program in its entirety, including credit origination, land-parcel eligibility determinations, marketing and broker placement activity, and related investor, banking, and tax records.

Where the subpoena's scope differs from the privilege analysis below, refer to the Responsiveness Definition for scope-specific guidance. Privilege and responsiveness are assessed independently (Section VI).

II. Legal standard

A document is protected by attorney-client privilege when all three of the following elements are satisfied. All three are mandatory — satisfying one or two is not sufficient.

A. Confidential communication

The communication was made with the intention of confidentiality and has been kept private. Sharing it with, or making it in the presence of, anyone outside the privileged circle defined in Section III generally destroys the privilege.

B. Between privileged persons

The communication occurred between CTH (acting through its personnel) and its attorneys, or the attorneys' agents (paralegals, associates, or other agents retained to assist with legal work). Being between privileged persons alone does not establish privilege — the purpose element (Section II.C) must independently be satisfied.

C. For the primary purpose of legal advice

The primary reason for the communication was to seek or provide legal assistance. This is presumed for substantive communications between CTH personnel and its counsel, unless the communication primarily relates to:

— Business, operational, or financial matters (e.g., budget approvals, staffing, scheduling)

— Administrative transmittals with no legal analysis (e.g., "here's the engagement letter," "please sign and return")

— Preservation/compliance directives issued company-wide (e.g., legal hold notices — see Rule V.C)

— Factual reporting that has not yet been analyzed or advised upon by counsel (see Rule V.B)

III. Privileged parties in this matter

In-house counsel: John Ellery, Head of Legal, Cascade Timber Holdings.

— Grace Lin — Partner

— Mia Chen — Associate

— Alan Brooks — Paralegal

Client organization (Cascade Timber Holdings personnel): Elena Marlowe (CEO), Robert Denniston (CFO), Sarah Nguyen (Chief Compliance Officer), Marcus Webb (Board Chair), Frank Delgado (VP Investor Relations), Craig Sato (Controller), Dan Osei (IT Director), Wendy Park (HR Director), and CTH's Board of Directors.

Any attorney above can independently create a privileged communication with any member of the client organization. No single attorney's presence is required to establish privilege — the analysis runs off the roles above, not any one person's name.

IV. Non-privileged third parties

Alder Point Partners and Bellhaven Advisory are separate companies, not part of CTH's privileged circle. Their personnel are not counsel for CTH or for each other in this matter:

— Alder Point Partners: Priya Shah, Tom Reyes, Jay Whitfield (aka "Kane"), Nina Alvarez

— Bellhaven Advisory: Derek Holt, Renee Ford

Their presence on an otherwise-privileged CTH email (e.g., Ellery or L&L Associates on the thread) vitiates privilege for that communication. There is no joint-defense or common-interest agreement between CTH and Alder Point Partners or Bellhaven in this matter — to the contrary, CTH's internal review examines whether Alder Point's and Bellhaven's own conduct exposed CTH to liability, so their interests are not aligned with CTH's for privilege purposes.

B. Factual reporting is not yet legal advice

A report that triggers a later privileged response is not itself privileged if it contains no legal advice.

C. Legal hold notices are administrative, not privileged

D. Engagement letters are administrative; the cover email may not be

E. Legal strategy discussion is privileged even when it touches budget

F. Document family independence

Each item in a document family (email plus attachments) is evaluated on its own content. A privileged cover email does not automatically make an attachment privileged, and vice versa. Apply this whenever an email attaches a spreadsheet, deck, or PDF — assess the attachment's own content for legal advice independent of the cover email.

G. No attorney involved means no privilege

If no CTH attorney (Ellery) and no L&L Associates attorney or agent participates in a communication — even if the subject matter is the Program or the internal review — the communication cannot be privileged. The topic alone does not create privilege.

VI. The Kovel agent doctrine

A. Legal standard

Under *United States v. Kovel*, 296 F.2d 918 (2d Cir. 1961), attorney-client privilege can extend to communications with a non-lawyer third party who is retained by the attorney (not the client) to help the attorney render legal advice — for example, an accountant retained by counsel to translate financial data into terms the attorney can use to give legal advice. The doctrine does not create a freestanding privilege for the third party; it treats the third party as functionally part of the attorney's team for the limited purpose of facilitating legal advice.

A person or vendor qualifies as a Kovel agent only if all of the following are true:

— Retained by the attorney (or at the attorney's direction), not retained directly by the client for an independent business purpose

— The vendor's role is to help the attorney understand facts or perform tasks necessary to render legal advice, not to provide the client with ordinary business, operational, or compliance services

— The communications at issue are within the scope of that legal-facilitation role, not general business correspondence that happens to pass through the vendor

Do not presume Kovel status from a vendor's mere presence on a Program-related communication. The presumption runs the other way: absent evidence the vendor was engaged by counsel to facilitate legal advice, treat the vendor as an ordinary third party whose presence vitiates privilege under Section IV.

This Option Agreement (this "Agreement") is made effective as of [____________], 2022 (the "Effective Date") by and between CLEARWATER LAND LLC, an Oregon limited liability company ("Owner"), and ALDER POINT PARTNERS, with offices in Sacramento, California ("Optionee"). Owner and Optionee are each a "Party".

RECITALS

A. Owner is the owner of certain real property in Klamath County, Oregon, located east of U.S. Highway 97 (the "Route 97 corridor"), containing approximately 148.62 acres according to the records of the Klamath County Assessor, and more particularly described in Exhibit A (together with all easements, rights and appurtenances, the "Property").

B. The Property adjoins other land of Owner to the south, which is the subject of a separate option agreement being negotiated between the Parties. This Agreement is independent of that agreement.

C. Optionee wishes to obtain, and Owner is willing to grant, an exclusive option to purchase the Property on the terms of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the Option Fee and the mutual covenants below, the Parties agree as follows:

1. Grant of Option

1.1 Owner grants to Optionee the exclusive and irrevocable option to purchase the Property on the terms of this Agreement (the "Option").

2. Option Term; Extension

2.1 The Option Term begins on the Effective Date and ends at 5:00 p.m. Pacific time on the day that is twelve (12) months after the Effective Date (the "Option Term").

2.2 Optionee may extend the Option Term once, for an additional period of six (6) months (the "Extension Period"), by written notice to Owner given before the Option Term expires, provided that each Option Payment then due has been paid or deferred under Section 3.3. References in this Agreement to the Option Term include any Extension Period.

3. Option Fee and Option Payments

3.1 In consideration of the Option, Optionee shall pay Owner an option fee of Twelve Thousand Dollars ($12,000) (the "Option Fee"), in installments (each, an "Option Payment") as set out in Schedule 1 below.

3.2 Option Payments shall be made by check or by wire transfer to an account designated by Owner in writing.

3.3 Optionee may, by written notice to Owner given on or before the due date of any Option Payment other than the Initial Option Payment, defer that Option Payment to a later date stated in the notice, which date shall be no later than the last day of the Option Term. Any Option Payment not paid by the last day of the Option Term is due on that day.

3.4 Optionee may prepay all or any part of the Option Fee at any time without premium or penalty.

3.5 Option Payments, once made, are non-refundable except as provided in Sections 6 and 10, and shall be credited against the Purchase Price at Closing.

Schedule 1 — Option Payments

Option Payment

Amount

Due (subject to Sections 3.3 and 3.4)

Initial Option Payment

$4,000

Within five (5) business days after the Effective Date

Second Option Payment

$4,000

On or before the 180th day after the Effective Date

Third Option Payment

$4,000

On or before the 270th day after the Effective Date

Total Option Fee

$12,000

4. Purchase Price

4.1 The purchase price for the Property is $1,150 per acre of Net Acreage (the "Purchase Price"), payable in cash at Closing, less the Option Payments made.

4.2 "Net Acreage" means the gross acreage of the Property as shown on the Survey, excluding any area within public road rights-of-way. The Assessor acreage stated in the Recitals and in Exhibit A is for identification only and is not a representation by either Party of Net Acreage.

5. Due Diligence; Survey

5.1 During the Option Term, Optionee and its consultants may enter the Property on reasonable prior notice to Owner to conduct boundary and topographic surveys, soil, environmental and siting studies and similar investigations, at Optionee's expense. Optionee shall repair any damage caused by its entry and shall indemnify Owner against third-party claims arising from it.

5.2 Optionee may obtain a boundary survey of the Property by a land surveyor licensed in Oregon (the "Survey").

5.3 Within fifteen (15) days after the Effective Date, Owner shall deliver to Optionee copies of any leases, surveys, title reports and recorded instruments affecting the Property that are in Owner's possession or control.

6. Title

6.1 Optionee may obtain a preliminary title report for the Property and shall notify Owner of any objections within thirty (30) days after receiving it. Owner shall notify Optionee within ten (10) days whether Owner will cure each objection. If Owner does not agree to cure an objection, Optionee may waive it or terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be refunded to Optionee.

6.2 Owner discloses that the Property, together with Owner's adjoining land, is subject of record to a grazing lease recorded in 1994 in Volume M94, Page 18832, Records of Klamath County, Oregon (the "Grazing Lease"). Owner represents that the Grazing Lease has expired by its terms and that no person holds grazing rights on the Property under it. No release of the Grazing Lease has been located of record. Before Closing, Owner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and record a release or quitclaim of the Grazing Lease from the lessee or its successors. If no release is recorded before Closing, Optionee may (a) waive this requirement, (b) extend Closing by up to sixty (60) days to allow it to be recorded, or (c) terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be refunded to Optionee.

7. Owner's Covenants

7.1 During the Option Term, Owner shall not sell, lease, encumber or grant any interest in the Property, or permit any lien to attach to it, without Optionee's prior written consent; provided that Owner and its members may continue the existing agricultural and grazing use of the Property until Closing, so long as that use does not interfere with Optionee's investigations under Section 5.

7.2 Owner shall keep the Property in its present condition, ordinary wear and natural causes excepted.

8. Exercise of Option

8.1 Optionee may exercise the Option at any time during the Option Term by written notice to Owner (the "Exercise Notice"). If the Option is not exercised before the Option Term expires, the Option shall lapse and Owner shall retain the Option Payments made.

9. Closing

9.1 Closing of the purchase shall occur through escrow with a title company in Klamath County, Oregon selected by Optionee, on a date designated by Optionee not later than sixty (60) days after the Exercise Notice ("Closing").

9.2 At Closing, Owner shall convey the Property to Optionee or its assignee by statutory warranty deed, subject only to exceptions approved or waived under Section 6. Owner shall pay the premium for a standard owner's policy of title insurance; escrow fees shall be shared equally; real property taxes shall be prorated as of Closing.

10. Termination; Default

10.1 Optionee may terminate this Agreement at any time by written notice to Owner. Owner shall retain the Option Payments made through the date of termination, except where termination results from Owner's default or a title failure under Section 6.

10.2 If Optionee fails to make an Option Payment when due (as it may be deferred under Section 3.3), Owner may give Optionee written notice of the failure. If the payment is not made within ten (10) days after that notice, Owner may terminate this Agreement by further written notice.

10.3 If Owner fails to perform under this Agreement, Optionee may seek specific performance or terminate this Agreement and recover all Option Payments made.

11. Memorandum of Option

11.1 On request of either Party, the Parties shall sign a memorandum of this Agreement in recordable form, which Optionee may record in the Official Records of Klamath County, Oregon.

12. Assignment

12.1 Optionee may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any affiliate of Optionee or to any successor to Optionee's land acquisition business, on written notice to Owner. Owner may not assign this Agreement without Optionee's written consent.

13. Notices

13.1 Notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with a copy by first-class mail, to the addresses below (or another address a Party designates by notice):

To Owner: Clearwater Land LLC, Attn: Gordon L. Pruitt, Managing Member, P.O. Box 1187, Klamath Falls, Oregon 97601; with a copy to Margaret A. Oyler, Oyler & Beck LLP, 412 Main Street, Klamath Falls, Oregon 97601

To Optionee: Alder Point Partners, Attn: Tom Reyes, Land Acquisition Manager, Sacramento, California; email: treyes@alderpointpartners.com

14. Governing Law; Venue

14.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Oregon. Any action arising under this Agreement shall be brought in the Circuit Court of the State of Oregon for Klamath County.

15. Miscellaneous

15.1 This Agreement is the entire agreement of the Parties regarding the Property and may be amended only in a writing signed by both Parties. Time is of the essence. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, and signatures delivered by scanned copy are effective as originals.

15.2 BEFORE SIGNING OR ACCEPTING THIS INSTRUMENT, THE PERSON TRANSFERRING FEE TITLE SHOULD INQUIRE ABOUT THE PERSON'S RIGHTS, IF ANY, UNDER ORS 195.300, 195.301 AND 195.305 TO 195.336. THIS INSTRUMENT DOES NOT ALLOW USE OF THE PROPERTY IN VIOLATION OF APPLICABLE LAND USE LAWS AND REGULATIONS (ORS 93.040).

Work product doctrine definition

Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc.

Version

v1.0 — prepared July 16, 2026

I. Applicable matter

This definition applies to materials prepared by or for Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc. or its representatives in anticipation of litigation or a government proceeding concerning the Coastal Solar Credit Program.

II. Legal standard

The work product doctrine protects documents and tangible things prepared in anticipation of litigation or for trial by or for a party or its representative (including attorneys, consultants, or agents), regardless of whether an attorney authored the material. Unlike attorney-client privilege, work product does not require an attorney to be a participant in the communication — it requires only that the material was prepared because of anticipated litigation or a government proceeding, and not in the ordinary course of business.

Two tiers apply:

— Fact work product — factual investigation/compilation material (lower protection; discoverable on a substantial-need/undue-hardship showing).

— Opinion work product — material reflecting the mental impressions, legal theories, or strategy of counsel (near-absolute protection).

III. Anticipation-of-litigation trigger date

Materials created before the trigger date below are ordinary-course business records, even if they later become important evidence. Materials created at or after the trigger date, because of the anticipated proceeding, are work product candidates.

TRIGGER DATE — FEBRUARY 24, 2023

E. Ambiguous business analysis — flag for human review

V. Work product and privilege are independent

VI. Waiver

Work product protection is waived when the material is disclosed to an adversary or to a third party without a shared interest in maintaining confidentiality — including disclosure to the IRS, or to Alder Point Partners/Bellhaven Advisory personnel, who are not part of CTH's defense team (see the Attorney-Client Privilege Definition, Section IV).
