B. The Property adjoins other land of Owner to the south, which the Parties expect to make the subject of a separate option agreement. This Agreement is independent of that agreement.

C. Optionee wishes to obtain, and Owner is willing to grant, an exclusive option to purchase the Property on the terms of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the Option Fee and the mutual covenants below, the Parties agree as follows:

1. Grant of Option

1.1 Owner grants to Optionee the exclusive and irrevocable option to purchase the Property on the terms of this Agreement (the "Option").

2. Option Term; Extension

2.1 The Option Term begins on the Effective Date and ends at 5:00 p.m. Pacific time on the day that is twelve (12) months after the Effective Date (the "Option Term").

2.2 Optionee may extend the Option Term once, for an additional period of six (6) months (the "Extension Period"), by written notice to Owner given before the Option Term expires, provided that each Option Payment then due has been paid or deferred under Section 3.3. References in this Agreement to the Option Term include any Extension Period.

3. Option Fee and Option Payments

3.1 In consideration of the Option, Optionee shall pay Owner an option fee of Twelve Thousand Dollars ($12,000) (the "Option Fee"), in installments (each, an "Option Payment") as set out in Schedule 1 below.

3.2 Option Payments shall be made by check or by wire transfer to an account designated by Owner in writing.

3.3 Optionee may, by written notice to Owner given on or before the due date of any Option Payment other than the Initial Option Payment, defer that Option Payment to a later date stated in the notice.

3.4 Optionee may prepay all or any part of the Option Fee at any time without premium or penalty.

3.5 Option Payments, once made, are non-refundable except as provided in Sections 6 and 10, and shall be credited against the Purchase Price at Closing.

5. Due Diligence; Survey

5.1 During the Option Term, Optionee and its consultants may enter the Property on reasonable prior notice to Owner to conduct boundary and topographic surveys, soil, environmental and siting studies and similar investigations, at Optionee's expense. Optionee shall repair any damage caused by its entry and shall indemnify Owner against third-party claims arising from it.

5.2 Optionee may obtain a boundary survey of the Property by a land surveyor licensed in Oregon (the "Survey").

5.3 Within fifteen (15) days after the Effective Date, Owner shall deliver to Optionee copies of any leases, surveys, title reports and recorded instruments affecting the Property that are in Owner's possession or control.

6. Title

6.1 Optionee may obtain a preliminary title report for the Property and shall notify Owner of any objections within thirty (30) days after receiving it. Owner shall notify Optionee within ten (10) days whether Owner will cure each objection. If Owner does not agree to cure an objection, Optionee may waive it or terminate this Agreement, in which case all Option Payments made shall be refunded to Optionee.

6.2 [Owner to confirm whether the old grazing lease on the Property was ever released of record. If not released, add Owner obligation to obtain and record a release before Closing.]

7. Owner's Covenants

7.1 During the Option Term, Owner shall not sell, lease, encumber or grant any interest in the Property, or permit any lien to attach to it, without Optionee's prior written consent.

7.2 Owner shall keep the Property in its present condition, ordinary wear and natural causes excepted.

8. Exercise of Option

8.1 Optionee may exercise the Option at any time during the Option Term by written notice to Owner (the "Exercise Notice"). If the Option is not exercised before the Option Term expires, the Option shall lapse and Owner shall retain the Option Payments made.

9. Closing

9.1 Closing of the purchase shall occur through escrow with a title company in Klamath County, Oregon selected by Optionee, on a date designated by Optionee not later than sixty (60) days after the Exercise Notice ("Closing").

9.2 At Closing, Owner shall convey the Property to Optionee or its assignee by statutory warranty deed, subject only to exceptions approved or waived under Section 6. Owner shall pay the premium for a standard owner's policy of title insurance; escrow fees shall be shared equally; real property taxes shall be prorated as of Closing.

10. Termination; Default

10.1 Optionee may terminate this Agreement at any time by written notice to Owner. Owner shall retain the Option Payments made through the date of termination, except where termination results from Owner's default or a title failure under Section 6.

10.2 If Optionee fails to make an Option Payment when due (as it may be deferred under Section 3.3), Owner may give Optionee written notice of the failure. If the payment is not made within ten (10) days after that notice, Owner may terminate this Agreement by further written notice.

10.3 If Owner fails to perform under this Agreement, Optionee may seek specific performance or terminate this Agreement and recover all Option Payments made.

11.1 On request of either Party, the Parties shall sign a memorandum of this Agreement in recordable form, which Optionee may record in the Official Records of Klamath County, Oregon.

12. Assignment

12.1 Optionee may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any affiliate of Optionee or to any successor to Optionee's land acquisition business, on written notice to Owner. Owner may not assign this Agreement without Optionee's written consent.

Portland, Oregon (“Seller”), acting through Alder Point Partners, with offices in Sacramento,

purposes of Sections 8 and 9, Bellhaven Advisory, with offices in Denver, Colorado (“Placement
Agent”).
RECITALS

“Program”), which Administrator administers on Seller's behalf (the “Credits”).
B. Administrator has engaged Placement Agent, on a non-exclusive basis, to market and broker
placements of Credits under a Broker Placement Agreement dated as of September 2, 2022.

set forth in Schedule 1, on the terms of this Agreement.
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set forth herein, the parties agree as
follows:
1. Definitions
“Face Amount” means the stated dollar value of a Credit as shown on its Credit Certificate. “Credit
Certificate” means the certificate issued under the Program evidencing a Credit. “Program
Documentation” means the Program description, investor deck, one-page summary, eligibility
checklist and eligibility screening materials prepared and furnished by Administrator, in the versions
approved by Administrator and delivered to Purchaser. “Closing” means the date on which Purchaser
pays the Aggregate Purchase Price. “Business Day” means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or bank
holiday in Portland, Oregon.
2. Purchase and Sale
Subject to the terms of this Agreement, Seller agrees to sell and Purchaser agrees to purchase Credits
having the aggregate Face Amount set forth in Schedule 1 (the “Purchased Credits”).
3. Purchase Price
The purchase price for the Purchased Credits is $0.89 per $1.00 of Face Amount (the “Unit Price”), for
an aggregate purchase price of $979,000 (the “Aggregate Purchase Price”), payable at Closing by wire
transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated in writing by Administrator.
Placement Agent's compensation is payable by Administrator under the Broker Placement Agreement
and is not payable by Purchaser.
4. Delivery of Credit Certificates
Within ten (10) Business Days after Closing, Administrator shall deliver to Purchaser, by electronic
transmission with originals to follow, Credit Certificates evidencing the Purchased Credits, each
identifying the certificate number, Program vintage, source parcel reference and Face Amount. Title to
and risk of the Purchased Credits pass to Purchaser upon delivery of the Credit Certificates. If any
Credit Certificate is not delivered within thirty (30) Business Days after Closing, Purchaser may, by

Certificates, that:
(a) Seller has full authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, and Administrator is
authorized to act for Seller in connection with the Program;
(b) the Purchased Credits are free of liens and have not been previously sold, assigned or pledged;
and
(c) in reliance on the eligibility screening performed by Administrator and on the Program
Documentation, including the eligibility checklist furnished with Administrator's approved

including Oregon and Washington.

this Agreement and the Program Documentation; and that it has full authority to enter into this
Agreement.

If any Purchased Credit is disallowed, reduced or determined ineligible under the Program or by any
taxing authority (a “Disallowance”), Purchaser may deliver a written refund request, with reasonable
supporting documentation, to Administrator within one hundred twenty (120) days after Purchaser
receives notice of the Disallowance (a “Refund Request”).
Within thirty (30) days after receipt of a timely Refund Request, Seller shall, at its election, (a) deliver
replacement Credits of equal Face Amount and like vintage, or (b) refund to Purchaser the Unit Price
multiplied by the disallowed Face Amount.
The remedies in this Section 7 and in Section 4 are Purchaser's sole and exclusive remedies for a
Disallowance or failure of delivery; in no event shall Seller's aggregate liability under this Agreement
exceed the Aggregate Purchase Price actually paid, and no party shall be liable for consequential,
incidental or punitive damages. This Section 7 survives Closing for four (4) years.

The Purchased Credits are offered and placed to Purchaser at its principal office in Oregon through
Placement Agent, acting solely as placement agent for Administrator. Purchaser acknowledges that

no representation or warranty regarding the Credits, the Program or the Program Documentation.
Placement Agent shall have no liability to Purchaser under Section 7.
9. Notices
Notices shall be in writing and delivered by email with confirmation copy by overnight courier: if to

Responsiveness definition

Matter

Version

v1.0 — prepared July 16, 2026

I. Purpose

This document defines what makes a record responsive to the IRS summons issued under 26 U.S.C. § 7602 (Case No. EX-2023-04471; called “the subpoena” in the corpus and below) issued to Cascade Timber Holdings, Inc. regarding the Coastal Solar Credit Program. A reviewer (human or LLM) must classify each document as RESPONSIVE or NOT RESPONSIVE and, if responsive, identify which of the five categories below (1–5) it falls under. A document may satisfy more than one category.

The subpoena defines its scope by subject matter — the Program and its surrounding relationships and records — not by custodian, sender, or date alone. A document is responsive because of what it discusses, not who wrote it.

II. Scope categories (subpoena document requests 1–5)

Category 1 — Tax-credit transactions

Records regarding tax-credit transactions involving renewable energy and land conservation programs, including credit origination, eligibility determinations, and transaction structuring documents.

Category 2 — Marketing and sales materials

Marketing and sales materials for the Program, including broker network materials, investor-facing decks, and sales communications distributed in 2022 and 2023.

Category 3 — Investor, buyer, seller, land trust, and advisor relationships

Records reflecting relationships with investors, buyers, sellers, land trusts, and advisors in connection with the Program, including engagement letters, correspondence, and agreements.

Category 4 — Alder Point Partners-affiliated entities and brokers

Records concerning corporate entities affiliated with Alder Point Partners, including organizational documents, ownership records, and inter-company agreements, together with any records concerning brokers engaged in connection with the Program, including Bellhaven Advisory.

Category 5 — Tax, accounting, banking, and loan records

Tax, accounting, banking, and loan records connected to the Program, including general ledger entries, bank statements, loan agreements, and tax filings referencing Coastal Solar credit transactions.

III. Not responsive

— Calendar invites, out-of-office autoreplies, IT security notices, HR announcements, expense/travel emails, and general unrelated chatter with no connection to the Program.

IV. Privilege is assessed separately

A document can be both responsive and privileged (produced on a privilege log, not in the production set). See the Attorney-Client Privilege Definition and Work Product Definition for that independent analysis. Responsiveness alone does not resolve whether a document must be produced.
